# Executive Summary
The Report Attribute Analyzer is a client-facing web application developed under the C5i BI Rationalization Suite — a product line by Course5 Intelligence (C5i) designed to help organizations govern and rationalize their Business Intelligence assets. The tool's primary purpose is to analyze Power BI report metadata, detect duplicate or semantically similar report attributes across multiple reports, and surface governance insights that enable BI teams to consolidate redundant content, reduce report sprawl, and improve data asset quality.
At its core, the application accepts Power BI metadata exports in Excel or CSV format, performs cross-report attribute matching, and applies LLM-powered similarity scoring to identify reports and fields that are functionally equivalent or overlapping — even when they differ in naming convention or phrasing. Results are presented in an interactive, filterable interface and can be exported back to Excel for downstream governance workflows. This positions the tool as a practical accelerator for BI portfolio rationalization initiatives, reducing the manual effort typically required to audit large report catalogs.
The technology stack is intentionally lightweight and front-end-only. The user interface is built with HTML5, Bootstrap 5.3.3 (loaded via CDN), and a custom CSS design system defined in style.css. The UI follows a structured component model with reusable elements including content cards (.content-card), a drag-and-drop file upload zone (.drop-zone), tabbed report cards (.card-tab-btn), sortable data tables (.data-table), and a live search interface (#search-input). The visual design uses a purple-dominant brand palette consistent with C5i's corporate identity, with full responsive support down to 480px viewport widths.
Architecturally, the application is a single-page application (SPA) delivered as a static web artifact (index.html + style.css), requiring no server-side runtime or database infrastructure for the UI layer. The LLM-powered similarity scoring referenced in the hero statistics implies integration with an AI/ML backend or API service, though the front end is decoupled from that concern. This architecture makes the tool straightforward to host, version, and embed within existing enterprise BI portals or internal tooling platforms. The maximum content width is constrained to 1200px, ensuring readability on standard enterprise desktop displays while remaining functional on tablet and mobile form factors.

# AI/ML Pipeline
This application implements a hybrid AI/ML pipeline for semantic attribute matching across PowerBI reports. The pipeline combines classical machine learning techniques (TF-IDF with cosine similarity) with a large language model (LLM) via Azure AI services to identify semantically equivalent column/attribute names across different reports.

### Overview
The pipeline operates in two stages:
Local ML Stage — Fast, deterministic similarity scoring using TF-IDF and string-distance metrics.
LLM Stage — Contextual semantic scoring via an Azure-hosted LLM for pairs that require deeper semantic understanding.

### Models Used
1. TF-IDF Vectorizer (scikit-learn)
Built using sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer with the following configuration:
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
analyzer='char',
ngram_range=(2, 4),   # Character bi-grams to 4-grams
lowercase=True,
min_df=1
)
Purpose: Captures sub-word character patterns to handle abbreviations, formatting differences, and partial name matches.
Similarity metric: Cosine similarity via sklearn.metrics.pairwise.cosine_similarity.
Scope: Fitted globally across all attributes from all reports at request time (no pre-trained model artifact is persisted to disk).
2. Azure-Hosted LLM — Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
Model: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
Endpoint: https://c5-ai-dataquality-foundary.services.ai.azure.com/
API Version: 2024-05-01-preview
Client: openai.AzureOpenAI
Purpose: Semantic disambiguation for attribute pairs that pass a preliminary similarity threshold but require contextual reasoning (e.g., Revenue vs Total Sales, CustID vs Customer ID).

### Data Pipeline and Preprocessing
Input Data
The pipeline ingests a tabular file (Excel/CSV) uploaded via the /find_overlaps route. The relevant columns are:
Attribute Construction
Attributes are constructed in Table.Field format (referred to as E.D format):
df['attribute_ed'] = (
df[new_semantic_table_col].astype(str).str.strip()
+ '.'
+ df[new_field_name_col].astype(str).str.strip()
)
Normalization
All attribute strings pass through the normalize() function before vectorization:
def normalize(text):
return (
str(text)
.replace("\u00A0", " ")   # non-breaking space
.replace("\u200B", "")    # zero-width space
.strip()
.lower()
)
Null, empty, and placeholder values (nan, none, nan.nan) are filtered out before processing.

### Training Process
There is no offline training phase. The TF-IDF vectorizer is fitted at runtime on each request using the full corpus of attributes extracted from the uploaded file:
all_attributes = []
for report_attrs in reports.values():
all_attributes.extend(report_attrs)
vectorizer, tfidf_matrix, attr_to_idx = build_tfidf_vectorizer(all_attributes)
The build_tfidf_vectorizer() function in server.py returns:
vectorizer — the fitted TfidfVectorizer instance
tfidf_matrix — the sparse document-term matrix for all attributes
attr_to_idx — a dictionary mapping each attribute string to its row index in the matrix
A fallback path returns (None, None, None) if the corpus is empty or vectorization fails.

### Hybrid Scoring
The calculate_hybrid_match_score() function combines three similarity signals with configurable weights defined in the WEIGHTS constant:
WEIGHTS = {
'jaccard': 0.30,    # Character-level n-gram similarity
'edit_dist': 0.25,  # Normalized edit distance (Levenshtein)
'tfidf': 0.45       # TF-IDF cosine similarity
}
`jaccard_similarity()` — Computes Jaccard similarity over character trigrams (n=3). Handles abbreviations and short tokens.
`edit_distance_similarity()` — Normalized Levenshtein distance (1.0 - distance / max_len). Handles typos and formatting variations.
`tfidf_similarity_score()` — Cosine similarity between TF-IDF vectors for two attributes, looked up by index from the pre-built matrix.

### Inference Setup
LLM Inference via `batch_llm_contextual_scores()`
LLM calls are batched to reduce API round-trips. The default batch size is 25 pairs per request.
def batch_llm_contextual_scores(
pairs: List[Tuple[str, str]],
client: AzureOpenAI,
model: str,
batch_size: int = 25
) -> Dict[Tuple[str, str], float]:
Each batch constructs a numbered prompt instructing the model to return a JSON object mapping pair indices to semantic similarity scores (0.0–1.0):
{
"1": 0.95,
"2": 0.15,
...
}
LLM inference parameters:
Parallel Execution
Batches are processed concurrently using ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=2:
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
future_to_batch = {executor.submit(process_batch, batch): batch for batch in batches}
for future in as_completed(future_to_batch):
batch_results = future.result()
results.update(batch_results)
Rate Limit Handling
Exponential backoff with jitter is applied on 429 / RateLimitReached errors:
delay = base_delay * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1)
Up to max_retries = 3 attempts are made per batch. Pairs that fail all retries default to a score of 0.0.
Match Threshold
An LLM score of ≥ 0.95 is required for a pair to be accepted as a confirmed semantic match:
if llm_score >= 0.95:

summary: Single-page application (SPA) with static front-end only (index.html + style.css); no server-side runtime or database required for UI layer.
Back-end AI/ML pipeline runs in Python (server.py) exposing a /find_overlaps route accepting Excel/CSV uploads.
Hybrid similarity scoring combines TF-IDF cosine (45%), Levenshtein edit distance (25%), and Jaccard character trigrams (30%).
LLM stage uses Azure-hosted Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct via AzureOpenAI client; endpoint hardcoded with credentials in server.py — security risk.
LLM API version 2024-05-01-preview; batched at 25 pairs per request, parallelised with ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers=2).
LLM confirmation threshold is ≥0.95 similarity score; exponential backoff with jitter applied on rate-limit errors (max 3 retries).
TF-IDF vectorizer is fitted at runtime per request on uploaded data — no persisted model artifacts or offline training phase.
Input data model requires Table and Field name columns; attributes constructed as Table.Field strings and normalised before processing.
Front-end stack: HTML5, Bootstrap 5.3.3 (CDN), custom CSS; responsive down to 480px, max content width 1200px.
Key UI components: drag-and-drop file upload, tabbed report cards, sortable/filterable data tables, live search, Excel export for governance workflows.
Designed for enterprise BI governance — detects duplicate/semantically similar Power BI report attributes to reduce report sprawl.
Architecture supports embedding in existing enterprise BI portals; no back-end infrastructure dependency for the UI layer simplifies hosting.
